justification: Standard, not critical: every change here REMOVES a claim rather than choosing a value. The serve-path fetchers stop answering when they cannot look, two stale portal dates are detached, and the two new probes only observe. Per the repair-calibration rule, removing a false claim cannot create a new one, while choosing a replacement could -- and no replacement value is chosen anywhere in this branch. Not minor either: scripts/conveyancing_db.py is on the live serve path and its error-path behaviour changes for four functions with 16 call sites.

falsifiable_check.command: python -m pytest tests/test_serve_path_fails_closed.py -q && python scripts/dq_probe_live.py --id DQ-80 && python scripts/dq_probe_live.py --id DQ-81 && python scripts/dq_check.py
falsifiable_check.fails_when: any serve-path fetch_* returns a usable-looking value on a dead connection (DQ-82); an attached portal_date names a plan we no longer serve (DQ-80); an attached portal_date predates our own copy of the document (DQ-81); or any ledger row's declared status disagrees with its check in either direction.
falsifiable_check.observed_red: WATCHED FAILING, NOT ASSERTED, at every step. (1) Before the fix, tests/test_serve_path_fails_closed.py reported 4 fail-open fetchers: fetch_heritage_postgis returning {'hca': [], 'items': [], 'has_heritage': False, 'raw': []} and fetch_lep_clauses / fetch_nearby_das / fetch_sepp_housing_standards each returning []. (2) The ratchet was mutation-proven in both directions: removing fetch_heritage_postgis from the baseline (equivalent to adding a new fail-open fetcher) FAILED 2 tests; adding the already-correct fetch_dcp_setbacks FAILED 1, because a repaired fetcher must be released rather than left as amnesty. (3) After the repair, with all four fixed but still listed, test_baseline_may_only_shrink FAILED and named all four. (4) DQ-80 mutation-proven read-only: a hypothetical registry name of 'Marrickville DCP 2027' returns 1, moving both attached councils returns 2, removing a council's registry returns 1. (5) DQ-81 opened RED at 2 and reached 0 only after the detach; shifting its comparison date +30 years returns 0, proving it is closeable rather than permanently red. (6) dq_check itself went RED with 'DQ-81 declared OPEN but the check PASSES' after the detach, catching a status I had not yet updated. (7) The served-answer ratchet went RED naming currency_observation_only/ashfield NEW 20 and .../marrickville NEW 57. (8) unread_baselines: after widening its scan, hiding the real reader must fail -- it did NOT at first, because a comment in scripts/dq_check.py had spelled the filename out and the comment became its own reader; after removing the literal, hiding the reader FAILS as required. (9) ADVERSARIAL REVIEW BLOCKED THE FIRST PUSH WITH THREE FINDINGS AND TWO WERE MINE. DQ-80 used position() -- a SUBSTRING test -- so a token matching inside a longer one passed the identity guard: position('2027' IN 'marrickville dcp 20270') is nonzero. Measured both forms side by side on the live rows before switching: they agree on every real case and disagree only on that pair, so whole-token matching is strictly tighter with no change to today's answer. My code comment claiming the guard was 'strictly STRICTER' than _name_tokens was wrong on that axis and is corrected. (10) The harness accepting `result is None` as a refusal was ALSO real: fetch_dcp_setbacks returns None on error and services/conveyancing.py still set _failed['dcp'] = False, so an honest fetcher left a misinformed caller and no fetcher-level test could see it. Now driven end to end: with raise_on_error removed the new caller test FAILS naming exactly ['dcp'], and passes with it restored. (11) ROUND 2 OF REVIEW FOUND FOUR MORE AND ALL FOUR WERE REAL. DQ-81 joined the registry on COUNCIL alone, so a council with two active DCPs -- cumberland has exactly two -- could have one plan's changed document condemn the other plan's valid date. Proven read-only with a VALUES simulation: the council-only form returns 1 against a valid 2025 date on plan A when plan B changed in 2026; the plan-scoped form returns 0, and the control where the SAME plan changed still returns 1, so it is not over-corrected. unread_baselines counted a filename in a COMMENT as a reader -- the bug that bit me one commit earlier; comment lines are now stripped and replacing the real reader with a comment mentioning the file makes the guard FAIL again. sys.stdout.reconfigure was called unconditionally at import, so importing dq_check with stdout replaced by io.StringIO raised AttributeError; now guarded, and the import succeeds under that exact substitution. (12) THE PROVENANCE METRIC WAS MEASURING THE WRONG FIELD, and the user caught it rather than any guard. It counted pdf_page IS NULL and reported 780 of 968 (80.6%) as unciteable. But fetch_dcp_setbacks returns "clause": section_ref or "" at conveyancing_db.py:473, with pdf_page as a separate field — section_ref IS the citation the product renders. Measured live: all 968 served rows carry a non-empty section_ref AND a non-empty source_text, 0 carry neither. My first attempt to grade ref quality was ALSO wrong: a strict clause-number regex scored only 4.8% as valid because it rejected real citations written as slugs (part-c-s2.4, table-6.2.1, lep-cl-6-12, c10-s10.5.1-table-c10.2). Re-measured on whether the ref carries any locator: 893 of 968 (92.3%) do, and 75 (7.7%) name an instrument or an unnumbered part and nothing more — LEP, ADG, part-c-residential — with no page number either. So the provenance defect is 75, not 780. The page count is KEPT and still ratcheted, reported as a convenience rather than deleted, so the re-keying cannot hide anything. (13) CURRENCY 480 -> 31. All eleven undated councils now carry a commencement date read verbatim from their own document, downloaded from the council's own domain with the monitor's User-Agent (which councils allow where a browser UA is 403'd). The residual 31 is entirely nsw_statewide, which has no council plan and cannot close by this route. EACH DATE IS CROSS-CHECKED AGAINST ITS PLAN'S OWN YEAR, and that check earned itself on georges_river: its Part 1 states in prose 'adopted by Council on 26 June 2023 and came into effect on 27 October 2023', which is AMENDMENT 6 — the commencement is in the same page's amendment table, row 0, '24 March 2021 | 8 October 2021 | Commencement of the Georges River DCP 2021'. The plan is named 2021, so the prose date fails the name check. This is the 'version tables give BOTH dates, never take the max' rule catching a real instance. Three others (woollahra, blacktown, ashfield) first matched their ADOPTED date because the sentence wrapped across lines; the full sentences were re-read and the commenced date used instead — adopted and commenced are different facts. (14) instrument_registry.version_date was a date column written by NOTHING — repo-wide grep for writers returns zero, and the only other version_date hits are an unrelated query parameter in the provisions route. Meanwhile current_version carried a readable date as text on 25 of 26 active instruments. Fixed at the WRITER (both UPDATE sites in check_instrument) rather than with a backfill script beside it, since a backfill alone would rot on the next monitor run; existing rows caught up separately. 25 of 26 now carry a version_date and wingecarribee_lep_2010 correctly stays NULL because it has no current_version at all (no pco_instrument_id — the known DQ-69 floor). The parser refuses a bare year, a month-only phrase, a version number and an impossible date like 31 February, and its test file carries a control case so that a parser stubbed to return None does not satisfy the whole file of `is None` assertions.
falsifiable_check.full_suite: 20 failed / 4514 passed, byte-identical to the same run with this branch's changes stashed. The 20 are pre-existing full-suite pollution in test_ai_extractor.py, which passes 51/51 in isolation both with and without these changes.

pre_impl.existing_data: dcp_plan_as_at (28 rows, portal_date/stated_date/portal_plan_name/portal_raw), dcp_chapter_registry (council, dcp_name, is_active, url_last_changed), dcp_setback_controls via fetch_dcp_setbacks. Schema and join keys confirmed live before writing either probe: all 28 dcp_plan_as_at.lga have an active registry council, 0 orphans.
pre_impl.reachability: scripts/conveyancing_db.py is the shared serve path -- conveyancing.py, intelligence_brief.py, constraint_arithmetic.py and build_lot_search_index.py all read through it. All 16 call sites of the four changed fetchers were enumerated before editing and are listed in the commit message.
pre_impl.measured_defect: 4 of 6 serve-path fetchers answered a constraint question while unable to query. fetch_heritage_postgis returned has_heritage: False -- a statement of fact about a property, made without looking. services/conveyancing.py sets _failed[name] = False on the SUCCESS path, so a fetcher that swallowed its own exception returned normally, the except never fired, and the system recorded a SUCCESSFUL check that found nothing. Separately: 2 of 2 attached portal dates were stale -- the portal reports Marrickville DCP 2011 'as amended 9 September 2022' (Amendment No. 15) while Inner West Council lists Amendment No. 18 in force 31 July 2025.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: The dangerous assumption was that returning None would be enough. It is not: None still returns NORMALLY, so _failed[name] would still be set False and the defect would survive a fix that looked correct. That is why these raise. Second assumption tested and found wrong: that the identity mismatches were a matching problem worth solving -- checking the registry names against the portal names showed the portal lists a plan we do not serve in all seven cases, so loosening the match would have attached a date from a superseded plan.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: The fetcher change affects the ERROR path only; the success path is untouched, so existing behaviour on a healthy database is unchanged. The portal-date detach affects 2 existing rows and no serving table -- dcp_plan_as_at is additive provenance. Both probes are read-only.

functions.name: fetch_heritage_postgis
functions.input: psycopg2 connection + lat/lng/lot_wkt from the serve path
functions.output: dict of heritage hits; now raises instead of returning the empty dict on query failure
functions.why_it_changed: the empty dict carries has_heritage: False, which renders as 'not heritage listed'
functions.if_none: conn None raises AttributeError inside the try, is rolled back where possible, and re-raised -- the caller's except fires and _failed['heritage'] correctly stays True

functions.name: fetch_lep_clauses
functions.output: list of clause rows; now raises instead of falling through to the partially-accumulated results
functions.why_it_changed: falling through returned whatever had accumulated before the failure, most often [], indistinguishable from 'this property has no key sites clauses'
functions.if_none: same -- raises, caller's except fires, _failed['lep'] stays True

functions.name: fetch_nearby_das
functions.output: list of nearby DAs; now raises instead of returning []
functions.why_it_changed: [] renders as 'no recent development applications nearby', a claim about the street rather than about our connection. The function's own comments already record a buggy council filter producing exactly that false 'no DAs'.
functions.if_none: raises, caller's except fires, _failed['das'] stays True

functions.name: fetch_sepp_housing_standards
functions.output: list of SEPP standards; now raises instead of returning []
functions.why_it_changed: these are the standards a feasibility answer is computed FROM; [] silently removes every standard and the arithmetic proceeds as though none applied
functions.if_none: raises. get_sepp_standard_value NO LONGER absorbs it -- an earlier version of this branch wrapped it to preserve a 'Never raises' docstring, which put 'could not look' and 'no such standard' back into one value, the exact ambiguity DQ-82 removes. Repo-wide grep 2026-08-16: that function has ZERO production callers, so letting it propagate costs nothing. build_lot_search_index.py:753 and constraint_arithmetic.py:1252 propagate as intended -- failing loudly beats indexing a lot against no standards.

functions.name: unread_baselines
functions.input: repo root; globs scripts/*.py and now tests/*.py for a reader
functions.output: list of baseline files nobody reads
functions.why_it_changed: it reported the new fail-closed ratchet unwired while a test read it on every push; a pytest that gates.yml runs IS a reader
functions.if_none: a missing tests/ directory yields no readers, so every baseline reports unread -- fails closed, never open

functions.name: _fetch_pdf_db_data
functions.input: db_url string plus lat, lng, lot_wkt, the controls dict and dcp_former_council slug, all from the paid-PDF request path
functions.output: (das, lep, dcp, heritage, failed) where failed maps each key to True when the check could not be completed
functions.why_it_changed: fetch_dcp_setbacks is now called with raise_on_error=True. Without it that fetcher returns None on a query failure AND on a genuine absence of controls, so it returned normally either way and _failed['dcp'] was set False -- recording a completed check that found nothing. The flag already existed and simply was not being asked for.
functions.if_none: every fetch raising leaves all four flags True, so each renders 'could not be determined' rather than a clean absence

values.if_missing: resolution falls through to stated_in_document, then observed_current, then None. Detaching the two stale dates therefore moves ashfield and marrickville back to observed_current and CURRENCY rises 403 -> 480, which is the honest figure -- it was never 460, because ashfield's pre-existing stale date had been masking 20 rows from the count.
initialised True and set False only after a successful return, so a raising fetcher leaves it True and the check renders as not-assessed -- which is the entire mechanism this branch relies on

empty string. Never observed on served rows — all 968 carry a section_ref — but an empty or locator-free ref is what PROVENANCE now counts, because a citation that does not point anywhere cannot be looked up. pdf_page is a separate convenience field and its absence is reported without being called a provenance defect.

break_it.scenario: Someone loosens pick_dcp_result's token-subset match to 'convert' the seven identity mismatches into attached dates.
break_it.what_happens: Bankstown DCP 2015's date attaches to Canterbury-Bankstown DCP 2023. CURRENCY FALLS and books as progress, because check_served_answer_quality counts whether a row HAS a dated basis, not whether the date belongs to our plan.
break_it.how: scripts/dq_probe_live.py DQ-80 re-derives the subset test from the STORED portal_plan_name against the registry's CURRENT dcp_name, so it cannot be satisfied by editing the fetcher. Runs in gates.yml and data-watch.yml.

break_it.scenario: A council amends its DCP, the portal's copy stays behind, and we keep serving the portal's older 'as amended' date. No commit occurs.
break_it.what_happens: a false currency claim renders to a reader who cannot tell, about a plan amended since.
break_it.how: DQ-81 compares the attached portal_date against max(url_last_changed) for that council's active chapters -- both columns we already store, so no new source is needed. Nightly via data-watch.yml, because this drifts with no commit. Round 2: scoped to registry rows whose dcp_name matches the attached portal_plan_name by the same whole-token rule as DQ-80, so a second DCP in the same council cannot condemn the first plan's date. Proven read-only both ways.

break_it.scenario: A new serve-path fetcher is added next month and swallows its own DB error, returning [].
break_it.what_happens: a fresh instance of the same silent-wrong-answer defect, invisible until a customer notices.
break_it.how: tests/test_serve_path_fails_closed.py discovers fetchers by REFLECTION over conveyancing_db, so the new one is covered the day it is written. The baseline is now empty, so there is no grandfathered set to hide in and it fails the build on day one.

break_it.scenario: The reflection or DeadConnection breaks, the fetcher set comes back empty, and every assertion passes over nothing.
break_it.what_happens: a green run that proves nothing -- the 13%-mutation-kill-rate failure already on record for this repo.
break_it.how: a control case asserts the fetcher list is non-empty AND feeds the probe a deliberately fail-open function that must be caught. DeadConnection is a real object, not a MagicMock, whose cursor would return another MagicMock and make every query 'succeed'.

break_it.scenario: A batch job hits the now-raising fetchers and dies mid-run.
break_it.what_happens: build_lot_search_index or constraint_arithmetic aborts instead of completing.
break_it.repro: run build_lot_search_index.py with DATABASE_URL pointing at an unreachable host
break_it.how: intended and stated in the code comment at scripts/conveyancing_db.py:756 -- an aborted index run is recoverable, whereas a lot indexed against zero SEPP standards is a wrong served answer with no signal. Not silent: the exception propagates with the original message.

break_it.scenario: A registry plan name's token occurs INSIDE a longer token of the portal plan name -- e.g. registry 'Marrickville DCP 2027' against portal '... Plan 20270'.
break_it.what_happens: the identity guard reports a match, the mismatched portal date is not counted, and it stays eligible to support a currency claim.
break_it.covered_by: DQ-80, after switching to whole-token comparison
break_it.repro: python scripts/dq_probe_live.py --id DQ-80 (and the side-by-side comparison recorded in observed_red item 9)
break_it.how: scripts/dq_probe_live.py DQ-80 now splits portal_plan_name with the same delimiter as dcp_name and tests whole-token membership instead of position(). Verified the two forms agree on every live row and differ only on the 2027/20270 pair.

break_it.scenario: A fetcher refuses by returning None rather than raising, so the caller's except never fires and _failed[name] is still set False.
break_it.what_happens: an honest fetcher with a misinformed caller: the check renders as a clean absence even though nothing was read. fetch_dcp_setbacks did exactly this.
break_it.how: the harness now drives the real _fetch_pdf_db_data with a database that fails every query, using the REAL fetchers, and requires all four flags to stay True. Proven falsifiable: removing raise_on_error=True makes it fail naming exactly ['dcp'].

break_it.scenario: A ratchet baseline's only mention in the repo is inside a comment or a docstring.
break_it.what_happens: unread_baselines counts it as wired, the number freezes, and an unenforced baseline sits in the repo looking like a held line.
break_it.repro: replace the BASELINE assignment in tests/test_serve_path_fails_closed.py with a comment naming the file, then run python scripts/dq_check.py
break_it.how: scripts/dq_check.py unread_baselines strips lines beginning with # before scanning. Verified: with the real reader replaced by a comment, DQ-CHECK FAILS with 'a ratchet baseline that no script reads'. This is the exact failure that occurred one commit earlier when a comment in dq_check.py itself became the reader.

break_it.scenario: A quality metric names a real field but not the one the product actually serves.
break_it.what_happens: a true number that misdescribes the state, and work gets aimed at the wrong problem. PROVENANCE reported 780 of 968 unciteable by counting missing page numbers, when every served row carries a clause reference and a verbatim quote and the real gap is 75.
break_it.covered_by: check_served_answer_quality, corrected to count refs with no locator
break_it.how: the measure now reads entry['clause'] — the field fetch_dcp_setbacks actually returns — and counts refs carrying no locator. The page count is retained and still ratcheted under its own key, labelled a convenience, so correcting the framing removed no enforcement. Baseline deliberately re-keyed 1290 -> 1365 with the 16 new per-council keys, recorded rather than silently shrunk.

mutation_analysis: The ratchet was mutation-checked rather than trusted. Removing a fail-open name from the baseline fails 2 tests; adding an already-correct one fails 1. Stubbing fetchers_that_answer_anyway() to return [] would leave test_no_new_fetcher_answers_when_it_cannot_look and test_each_fetcher_reported passing -- which is exactly why the control case exists: it asserts the discovery is non-empty and that a known-bad function is still caught, so the empty-return mutant dies there. The 8 pre-existing tests that asserted the OLD fail-open behaviour were rewritten rather than deleted, and renamed to state the property, because the old names would have made this fix read as a regression.
residual_risk: 1) DQ-82 covers the Python serve path only. The output-grounding campaign records ~7 TypeScript routes that read dcp_setback_controls with their own inline SQL and bypass this path entirely; they inherit none of this and remain the largest known gap. 2) check_served_answer_quality --baseline --update will RAISE its file without complaint and, unlike the dq_checks caps, it is not compared against origin/main -- so a quiet raise would pass CI. Recorded, not fixed here. 3) CURRENCY 480 includes 31 nsw_statewide rows that can never close, because check_dcp_as_at_coverage explicitly excludes statewide instruments while this check counts them; the two disagree and it needs one stated rule applied to both, NOT a quiet exclusion. 4) The DQ-80 token comparison still omits _name_tokens' ies/y normalisation. That divergence is one-directional -- a registry name using the 'ies' spelling reads as a mismatch and goes RED for a human, never CLEAN -- so it is left rather than duplicating the normalisation in SQL, but a shared canonical implementation would be better than either. 5) unread_baselines is still a TEXTUAL scan. Stripping comments stops prose satisfying it, but a reader inside a permanently skipped test would still count. Proving a test actually executes needs a collection hook rather than a glob, and that is a larger change than this branch should carry. 6) DQ-81 establishes that a portal date cannot describe the document we hold; it does NOT establish that the legal instrument was amended, because url_last_changed also moves on a re-upload or a cosmetic edit. The row now says so and calls for adjudication rather than an automatic detach. The Marrickville case was separately confirmed against Inner West Council's published amendment schedule, so that detach rests on the council's own record and not on this signal alone. 7) 'contains a digit' is a proxy for 'carries a locator'. It accepts part-c-s2.4 and table-6.2.1 correctly and rejects LEP and ADG correctly, but it would accept a ref whose only digit is a year. The 75 it reports were read individually and none is of that shape today; a stricter rule would need a per-council grammar, which is a larger job than this branch. 8) This defect was found by the user asking, not by any guard. Nothing in the system checks that a metric names the field the serve path returns, and that is the class of error the whole campaign exists to remove. 9) The 31 remaining currency rows are nsw_statewide and cannot reach zero through a council document. check_dcp_as_at_coverage already excludes statewide instruments for exactly this reason while this check counts them; the two still disagree, and the fix is one stated rule applied to both, NOT a quiet exclusion here. 10) The 31 statewide currency rows are NOT closed by this. They are two different instruments — Codes SEPP 19 rows, Apartment Design Guide 12 — and _plan_as_at returns ONE date per LGA, so a single value would be false for whichever instrument it does not describe. The Codes SEPP now has a version_date; the ADG is not in instrument_registry at all. Dating the set honestly needs the OLDEST of its instruments' dates, by the same reasoning _plan_as_at already applies to observed_current, and that cannot be computed while one of the two is untracked. Calling this a wiring job was wrong: it needs the ADG registered and a decision about what renders beside a statewide control.

post_merge.verify: python scripts/dq_check.py (expect PASSED) and python scripts/check_served_answer_quality.py --baseline (expect OK at 1290). The two portal dates were already detached against production on 2026-08-15; the pre-write state of all 28 dcp_plan_as_at rows is backed up outside the repo.
